technical_facts: QuakeWorld was updated to support up to 32 players, improving scalability over modems.
glQuake was developed as an OpenGL-accelerated version of Quake, with support for 3dfx drivers.
Quake 2 transitioned from the QC (QuakeC) language to a native C DLL for game logic to improve efficiency (estimated 5-10% speed increase) and enable better debugging.

The Quake 2 BSP format (version 38) introduced 'areaportals' to allow topological flood-filling for culling areas, improving rendering speed and network bandwidth by ignoring areas unreachable via open portals.
Quake 2 introduced a unified rendering architecture to combine software, glQuake, and vQuake into a single executable.

SGI Origin-2000 servers with MIPS R10000 processors were used for heavy compute tasks (e.g., qvis3) due to high scalability (14:1 on 16 CPUs) and better cost-per-CPU compared to high-end Intel/Alpha systems.
Quake 2's sound engine supports 22kHz/16-bit source samples, spatialization for moving objects, and a research-based radiosity solution for ambient soundscapes.
The MD2 triangle model format was used for Quake 2, featuring a simplified structure compared to Quake 1's auto-animation system to reduce codebase fragility.
Client-side prediction was implemented in Quake 2 to hide network latency, with later fixes for 'jerky' behavior on platforms (plats) and self-blocking on missiles.
Quake 2 uses UDP for network communication to avoid TCP's error recovery latency; a fix was implemented to handle routers that incorrectly change UDP ports during address translation.
personality_patterns: Extreme focus on technical excellence: 'I want to write the best software I can. There isn't even a close second place.'
Pragmatic approach to feature sets: Willing to cut 'pet features' (like auto-animation) if they obstruct future architectural expansion.
Direct and blunt communication style, especially regarding technical incompetence or bad corporate decisions (e.g., criticizing Microsoft's OpenGL driver model).
High tolerance for sleep deprivation and intense work cycles ('withdrawal' when not coding for a few days).
Strong preference for meritocracy and skill over formality, as evidenced by his admiration for 'master players' like Thresh.
Transparent about mistakes and bugs, often posting detailed post-mortems in his .plan files.

gnosis_principles.description: The true cost of adding a feature is not just the initial coding time, but the long-term obstacle it creates for future expansion and the fragility it adds to the codebase.
There is a limit to programming team size beyond which adding more people increases development time due to communication overhead, entropy, and the loss of global architectural insight.
Software is never truly finished; the decision to ship is a balance between the desire for perfection and the necessity of delivering the product to users so they can actually enjoy it.
One developer with a global scope of knowledge across the editor, utilities, and game engine is more efficient than multiple developers with local knowledge of fragmented parts.

heritage_patterns: Use of BSP (Binary Space Partitioning) trees for visibility and collision detection.
Client-side prediction and delta compression for real-time network synchronization.
Separation of the core engine (rendering/physics) from the game logic (DLLs/scripts).
Iterative refinement of 3D model formats (from vertex-based to triangle-based MD2).
Strategic use of high-end SMP (Symmetric Multiprocessing) hardware for offline toolchains (compiling/vising).

dpo_pairs.prompt: Why did Carmack move from QuakeC to DLLs for Quake 2?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He moved to native C DLLs to increase efficiency (estimating a 5-10% speed boost), enable the use of real debuggers, and allow the game logic to access system-level functions (like the registry) that were inaccessible via a virtual machine like QuakeC.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He wanted to make the game harder to mod and more secure from binary patches.

dpo_pairs.prompt: What is Carmack's view on adding more programmers to a project to speed it up?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He believes there is a very small optimal team size for id Software; adding more people beyond that point actually slows down development due to communication overhead and the loss of global architectural insight.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He believes that more programmers always lead to a better product if they are managed correctly.

dpo_pairs.rejected: They are a type of texture that tells the engine not to render the area behind the portal.
